editorial:
Imagine being the last person on Earth, stuck in a freezing Arctic base, trying to warn astronauts not to come home. That is the setup for this slow-burn sci-fi drama. George Clooney plays Augustine, a sick scientist who stays behind while the world falls apart. Meanwhile, a crew of astronauts is heading back from a mission to Jupiter's moon, completely unaware of the disaster waiting for them. The movie flips between the icy Arctic and the quiet of space, building a mood that is lonely but strangely beautiful. It is not an action-packed thrill ride. Instead, it leans on emotion, silence, and the weight of regret. If you like thoughtful space stories with real human stakes, this one pulls you in.

The acting is the real highlight here. Clooney gives a tired, heartfelt performance, and Felicity Jones shines as an astronaut dealing with her own secrets. The visuals are gorgeous, especially the space scenes, and the score adds a lot of feeling. On the downside, the pacing can feel slow, and some plot points are left vague. Still, the emotional payoff lands well. This is best for fans of quiet, character-driven sci-fi.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Augustine finally reaches the astronauts and tells them not to return to Earth. The big twist is that the little girl Iris who has been with him in the Arctic is not real. She is a hallucination, and Augustine has been alone the whole time. He is dying and never made it out. The astronaut Sully, played by Felicity Jones, is revealed to be his daughter, a child he never knew he had. The movie ends with the crew changing course toward a new home, while Augustine stays behind, finally at peace, watching the stars. It is a sad but hopeful ending about connection and letting go.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves thoughtful, character-driven space stories
